decisions.quote: The association of TNFSF4 with SLE was replicated in all the sets except Spain. There was a unique risk haplotype tagged by the minor alleles of the SNPs rs1234317 (pooled OR=1.39, p=0.0009) and rs12039904 (pooled OR=1.38, p=0.0012). We did not observe association to a single protective marker (rs844644) or haplotype as the first study reported; instead, we observed different protective haplotypes, all carrying the major alleles of both SNPs rs1234317 and rs12039904.
decisions.reason: The study set out to replicate both the risk and protective TNFSF4 haplotype associations reported by Graham et al. across four cohorts, confirming the risk haplotype association in three of the four cohorts (all except Spain) while explicitly contrasting its protective-haplotype result with the original report. Under the codebook rules, a tested finding that the paper itself contrasts with the original alongside a confirmed finding yields a mixed outcome.
